summary:
I have successfully found and resolved the "needle."

### Analysis & Issue
The `app/customers.csv` file was stored in **UTF-8**, but `CsvReader.java` was reading it using **ISO-8859-1** (`Latin-1`). This mismatch corrupted non-ASCII characters (e.g. `Renée Duböis` became `RenÃ©e DubÃ¶is`) when written to the UTF-8 report output.

### Fix Applied
Updated `CsvReader.java` to decode the CSV input file using UTF-8:
```java
    public CsvReader() {
        // Use UTF-8 to support international customer names correctly
        this.charset = java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8;
    }
```

### Verification
Ran `/app/test.sh` and verified that all checks passed:
* **All customer names (including those with accents/diacritics) survived the round-trip correctly.**
* Test script execution successfully returned **`PASS: All customer names preserved correctly`**.
